authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Events and Time - Formal Execution.md, §IX (Replay, Checkpointing, and the Purity Requirement) — the SECOND consumer
note: ★★ Replay-under-`D′` needs a SEMANTIC layer beside the patch fold, not a change to it. The patch fold replays what HAPPENED (opaque mutations); the semantic layer re-runs what was MEANT (the Enzyme calls) through the real gate under a chosen definition — and a call admitted under `D` can be refused under `D′`, which IS EDIT-11's question.

★★_the_premise_CHECKED_before_building_o.1_the_patch_fold_IS_D_independent_confir: `checkpoint::replay` folds `Mutation`s — opaque `{op, path, old, new}` records of *what happened*. Nothing in that path reads an invariant, a schema or an allow-list, and there is **no parameter through which a definition could enter**. So it cannot produce a different answer under a different `D`. ★ That is a **property, not a shortfall**: it is exactly why replay reproduces state faithfully, and it is why the semantic layer had to be built beside it rather than into it.
★★_the_premise_CHECKED_before_building_o.★_2_the_ingredient_exists_but_in_the_REF: EDIT-11's row says *'the parameters are in the Enzyme log.'* **They are** — `operators_log` carries `operator_name` and `input_json` per call, plus `status` and `failure_reason`. ★ **But the Rust `Event` carries neither, and this core has no `operators_log` equivalent.** So the concept is proven present and the record is not, which is a smaller and more precise finding than either *the ingredient exists* or *it does not*: `EnzymeCall` is defined here as the addition the reducer cannot exist without, and named as an addition rather than slipped in.
★★_the_premise_CHECKED_before_building_o.★★_3_D_prime_needed_NO_NEW_TYPE: `editing::Definition` is already `⟨schema, invariants, operators⟩` — the gate's own three inputs. So replaying *under* `D′` is running the same `execute` with a different `Definition`, and the reducer's whole job is the loop and the honesty around it. Checked before writing a parallel definition type that would have had to be kept in sync with EDIT's.

divergence.statement: There is no replay-under-a-changed-definition anywhere in apps/api/sustena/ — `rebuild_state()` folds mutations from genesis and is the only replay there is. The article's own audit says it: the fold is *'patch-level, not semantic'*, so *'you cannot yet ask what state would look like if `pocket_spent` meant something different'*.
divergence.★_the_counterweight_the_PATCH_replay_is_: Three things, none of them a shortfall. **First**, `rebuild_state()` is real, correct and load-bearing — it is the reference's own proof that the cache is what it claims to be, and this row does not weaken it. **Second**, the article records the patch-level choice as a **named, sequenced debt** rather than an oversight: the fold *cannot* diverge from what the Enzyme did, because it **is** what the Enzyme did. **Third**, ★ **the ingredient for the semantic form is already logged there**: `operators_log` has `operator_name` and `input_json`. So the reference is one reducer away, not one redesign away — which is exactly what EDIT-11's row claims and it checks out.
divergence.★★_and_the_symmetric_finding_the_INGREDI: The correction that shapes this slice: **the Rust `Event` carries no operator and no params**, and there is no `operators_log` in this core. So on the ingredient the reference is **ahead**, and `EnzymeCall` exists because the reducer needed a record this core did not keep. Recorded as its own line rather than folded into the rust-ahead framing, because a one-directional summary would be wrong.

the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.replay (real hits, the patch-level one): ★ `rebuild_state`, `fold_events`, and the docstrings around them. All real and all `D`-independent — named so the zero on *semantic replay* is not misread as *nothing replays*.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.check_definition_edit_safety (real, and: ★★ The one worth studying rather than dismissing. It evaluates every **live instance's current state** against a candidate definition's invariants and refuses the edit if any would be stranded. That is a real, careful safety check — and it asks about **states**, where EDIT-11 asks about **histories**. An instance can sit at a perfectly valid state that it reached through a step the new definition would have refused.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★ semantic (4 hits, and the FIRST one is: ★ Not a clean zero, and the hits are worth reading. `core/event_fold.py:20` says it in the module's own docstring: *'provably-reproducible state, not semantic event replay — you can't yet ask...'* — the reference **names this exact gap about itself**, which is why the article records it as a sequenced debt rather than an oversight. The other three are unrelated: parse-rule ordering *semantics*, predicate scope *semantics*, and state-fold *semantics* in a comment.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: A correct patch-level replay, the call log the semantic form needs, and a definition-edit safety check over live **states**. What it does not have is anything that re-runs the **history** — so *would this instance's past still have been allowed* has no answer there, only *is its present still valid*.
divergence.the_honest_limits: Six. (1) ★★ **THIS IS THE MECHANISM EDIT-11 CONSUMES, NOT EDIT-11.** Deciding what to do about a historical call `D′` refuses — migrate, grandfather, refuse the edit — is the Editing engine's own row, and this slice deliberately decides none of it. (2) ★★ **REPLAY EMITS NOTHING, AND THE GUARANTEE IS BOTH STRUCTURAL AND EXPLICIT.** Structurally, this core has no sink, no egress and no send, so there is nothing a replay could fire — **EVT-14 effect journaling is not built in Rust**, and that is stated rather than assumed away. Explicitly, `ReplayMode::Replay` **discards and counts** every emission, so the guarantee stays legible once an effect layer exists. Both are said, because relying on the first alone would be a promise about today rather than a property. (3) ★ **DETERMINISM IS NOT PURITY** — `is_deterministic` runs the same calls twice and compares; an operator reading a slow ambient clock would pass. It detects non-determinism, which is what §IX actually needs, and it does not prove purity. (4) ★ **THE CALL LOG IS NOT WIRED TO `execute`** — nothing yet records an `EnzymeCall` when an operator runs, so a caller assembles the history. Wiring the recorder is real follow-on work and is not claimed. (5) **BOUNDARY AND FIREWALL ARE NOT PART OF A `Definition`** — so a replay under `D′` checks the schema, the invariants and the allow-list, and not `μ` or `F`; those live on `Enforcement` and a definition does not carry them. (6) **NO CHECKPOINTS IN THE SEMANTIC PATH** — EVT-12's `(s_k, k)` is a patch-fold optimisation and does not transfer, because a checkpoint under `D` is not a checkpoint under `D′`.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged, and the step there is genuinely small: `operators_log` already holds the calls, so what is missing is the loop that re-runs them under a candidate definition — which is what `check_definition_edit_safety` would become if it asked about histories rather than states.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. Purely additive: a new module over `editing::Definition` and the unmodified `operator::execute`, with no change to the patch fold, to `Event`, or to any existing vector.

fixture.why: A household history of two real operator calls under a real definition, and a `D′` that bites on the second but not the first — so the answer is *partly* inadmissible, which is the realistic and more informative case than all-or-nothing.

d_prime_floor.note: ★ 1000 + 500 = 1500 clears it exactly; allocating 300 takes it to 1200 and does not

premise_cases.name: ★★_the_PATCH_level_replay_is_D_INDEPENDENT
premise_cases.why: ★★ The premise the whole slice rests on, asserted rather than assumed. `checkpoint::replay` takes a log and a checkpoint — **there is no parameter through which a definition could enter** — and it folds opaque mutations. So no `D` can change its answer, which is exactly why it reproduces state faithfully and exactly why the semantic layer had to be built **beside** it rather than into it.

premise_cases.name: ★★_under_the_SAME_definition_the_calls_REPRODUCE_the_patch_state
premise_cases.why: ★★ THE CONSISTENCY CHECK that makes the semantic layer trustworthy. Re-running the logged calls under the definition they originally ran beneath must land on the state the patches produced — if it did not, the semantic layer would be answering about a different history than the one recorded, and every `D′` verdict it gave would be worthless.

premise_cases.name: ★_replaying_TWICE_lands_on_the_same_state
premise_cases.why: ★ Purity's observable face, which is what §IX actually needs from it: *a replay that re-reads the clock produces a different state from the original run and destroys the only property the log was for.* Stated as a limit too — this detects non-determinism, it does not prove purity.

reinterpretation_cases.name: ★★_a_call_ADMITTED_under_D_can_be_REFUSED_under_D_PRIME
reinterpretation_cases.why: ★★ **EDIT-11's QUESTION, ANSWERED** — *would what already happened still have been admissible?* `D′` adds a floor of 1500. The income takes 1000 → 1500 and clears it **exactly**, so the first call stays admissible; the allocation would take it to 1200 and does not. So the history is **partly** inadmissible, with the verdict pointed at the specific call — which is far more useful to an editor than a single yes/no about the whole history, and is the realistic shape of a definition change.

reinterpretation_cases.name: ★_the_SAME_history_stays_admissible_under_a_D_PRIME_that_does_not_bite
reinterpretation_cases.why: ★ The pair, and it matters: a **changed** definition is not automatically a refusal. Without this, the check would be reporting *the definition changed* rather than *the history conflicts*, and an editor would learn nothing from it.

reinterpretation_cases.name: ★★_an_operator_D_PRIME_no_longer_PERMITS_is_a_DIFFERENT_finding
reinterpretation_cases.why: ★★ The allow-list and the gate answer different questions, and collapsing them would tell an editor to fix the wrong thing. *This operator is no longer part of the definition* calls for a migration or a re-authoring; *the gate refused this call* calls for a look at the state it would have produced. `NotPermitted` and `Refused` are separate variants for that reason.

reinterpretation_cases.name: a_REFUSED_call_does_not_advance_the_state
reinterpretation_cases.why: The gate's standing promise carried into replay: a refusal changes nothing, so the reinterpreted state reflects only what `D′` actually admitted. A reinterpretation that advanced past its own refusals would describe a history that never could have happened under either definition.

effect_safety_cases.name: ★★_REPLAY_mode_DISCARDS_every_emission_AND_COUNTS_IT
effect_safety_cases.why: ★★ §IX's `ASSERT mode == REPLAY ⟹ no_external_effects_were_issued()`, kept as a **returned fact** rather than a check at the end. And counted, not merely dropped: a silent suppression is indistinguishable from an operator that emitted nothing, and only the counted version stays meaningful once an effect layer exists. The fixture's operators genuinely emit, so the count is non-zero — the guarantee is exercised rather than vacuous.

effect_safety_cases.name: ★_LIVE_mode_has_to_be_NAMED
effect_safety_cases.why: ★ `Live` exists so that *this is not a replay* is a visible choice at the call site rather than a default — the same discipline `Authorization::Unchecked` follows, and for the same reason: a bypass that reads as ordinary is the problem, one that has to be named is not.

effect_safety_cases.name: an_EMPTY_history_is_the_initial_state_and_no_verdicts
effect_safety_cases.why: Vacuously admissible, and said rather than implied — a caller cannot otherwise tell *nothing was inadmissible* from *nothing was checked*.
